1.title: Score Gate: if
1.description: A practice quiz needs a `scoreLabel(score)` helper. Return "Pass" when the score is 60 or higher; otherwise return "Retry". Keep the boundary inclusive: a score of exactly 60 passes.
1.learningObjective: Use a one-way if branch to award a pass at the inclusive score threshold of 60.
instructions: Write the scoreLabel(score) function.
Add an if condition for score >= 60.
Return "Pass" for a passing score and "Retry" for a lower score.
Check both 59 and 60 to verify the boundary.

workedExample.explanation: Trace the condition with 60, then compare the returned result with the expected value.

1.hint: The threshold should be checked with >=. The branch can return immediately, so no extra variable is required.
1.explanation: An if branch runs only when its condition is true. Using >= includes the threshold itself, while the function’s final return covers the remaining scores.

6.title: Guest Name Fallback: logical OR
6.description: A profile card should display "Guest" when its nickname is empty. Implement `displayName(nickname)` with a logical OR fallback; a non-empty nickname must be returned unchanged.
6.learningObjective: Use a fallback expression for an empty display name while preserving a supplied name.
instructions: Create displayName(nickname).
Return nickname with "Guest" as the fallback.
Check both an empty string and a non-empty name.
Make sure the non-empty name is not replaced.

workedExample.explanation: Trace the condition with "Mira", then compare the returned result with the expected value.

6.hint: In JavaScript, an empty string is falsy, so nickname || "Guest" selects the fallback only for the empty case.
6.explanation: The || operator returns the first truthy operand, or the final operand when earlier values are falsy. It preserves a non-empty nickname.
